```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
```

```{r setup}
library(OncoCohortSelect)
```

This article analyzes the data of a completed trial with three single-arm
cohorts, with column names in the style of ADaM data sets. The data are
fictitious and are installed with the package.

## Data

The file has one row per patient: the cohort (`TRT01P`), the overall and
progression-free survival times in months (`OSAVAL`, `PFSAVAL`) with their
censoring indicators (`OSCNSR`, `PFSCNSR`; 0 for an event and 1 for a censored
time, as in ADaM), the best overall response (`BOR`) and a flag for an adverse
event of interest (`AEFL`, `"Y"` or blank).

```{r}
path <- system.file("extdata", "example_trial.csv", package = "OncoCohortSelect")
adsl <- read.csv(path, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
head(adsl)
table(adsl$TRT01P, adsl$BOR)
table(adsl$TRT01P, adsl$AEFL == "Y")
```

## Endpoints

`Endpoint()` names the columns of each endpoint. For a time-to-event endpoint,
`censor` gives a censoring indicator coded as in ADaM (0 for an event, any
other value for a censored time) and `event` an event indicator (1 for an
event). For a binary endpoint, `positive` lists the values that count as 1,
here a complete or partial response and the flag `"Y"`.

```{r}
eps <- list(
  Endpoint("OS", "tte", time = "OSAVAL", censor = "OSCNSR"),
  Endpoint("PFS", "tte", time = "PFSAVAL", censor = "PFSCNSR"),
  Endpoint("ORR", "binary", var = "BOR", positive = c("CR", "PR")),
  Endpoint("AE", "binary", var = "AEFL", positive = "Y", higher.better = FALSE))
```

In ADaM, time-to-event data are usually in a separate data set with one row
per patient and parameter. `reshape()` puts the parameters side by side, and
`merge()` adds them to the data of the patients:

```{r}
adtte <- data.frame(USUBJID = c("01", "01", "02", "02"),
                    PARAMCD = c("OS", "PFS", "OS", "PFS"),
                    AVAL = c(10.2, 5.1, 8.4, 8.4), CNSR = c(1, 0, 0, 0))
reshape(adtte, idvar = "USUBJID", timevar = "PARAMCD", direction = "wide")
```

The columns `AVAL.OS` and `CNSR.OS` are then given to `Endpoint()`.

## Benefit-risk scores

Against target values, with the criteria of the article *Evaluating decision
rules by simulation*:

```{r}
crit <- data.frame(endpoint = c("ORR", "PFS", "OS", "AE"),
                   target = c(0.30, 0.50, 0.60, 0.40), time = c(NA, 6, 12, NA),
                   weight = c(1 / 3, 1 / 3, 1 / 3, 1), cutoff = c(NA, NA, NA, 0.8))
br <- BenefitRisk(adsl, eps, crit, group = "TRT01P")
br
```

Relative to Cohort 1, the reference regimen:

```{r}
crit_ref <- data.frame(endpoint = c("ORR", "PFS", "OS", "AE"),
                       measure = c("rate", "hr", "hr", "rate"),
                       target = c(0.10, 0.80, 0.90, 0.10),
                       weight = c(1 / 3, 1 / 3, 1 / 3, 1), cutoff = c(NA, NA, NA, 0.8))
br_ref <- BenefitRisk(adsl, eps, crit_ref, group = "TRT01P", reference = "Cohort 1")
br_ref
```

## Win statistics

Each new cohort is compared with Cohort 1, with priority OS, PFS, response and
adverse event.

```{r}
w2 <- WinStat(adsl, eps, treatment = "Cohort 2", control = "Cohort 1", group = "TRT01P")
w3 <- WinStat(adsl, eps, treatment = "Cohort 3", control = "Cohort 1", group = "TRT01P")
w2$ci
w3$ci
```

The net treatment benefit against Cohort 1 is
`r round(w2$estimate[["ntb"]], 2)` for Cohort 2 and
`r round(w3$estimate[["ntb"]], 2)` for Cohort 3. With the scoring rule of
Péron, censored pairs are scored with the Kaplan-Meier estimates:

```{r}
rbind(
  "Cohort 2" = WinStat(adsl, eps, treatment = "Cohort 2", control = "Cohort 1",
                       group = "TRT01P", scoring = "peron")$estimate,
  "Cohort 3" = WinStat(adsl, eps, treatment = "Cohort 3", control = "Cohort 1",
                       group = "TRT01P", scoring = "peron")$estimate)
```

## Applying a decision rule

The decision rule and its threshold are fixed when the trial is designed, for
example with `CalibrateThreshold()` as in the article *Evaluating decision
rules by simulation*. `SimSelection()` computes all the statistics of a
completed trial when the data are treated as one simulated trial, and
`SelectionOC()` then gives a probability of 1 to the cohort that the rule
selects. The thresholds below are for illustration only.

```{r}
adsl$sim <- 1
res <- SimSelection(adsl, eps, crit, reference = "Cohort 1", criteria.ref = crit_ref,
                    group = "TRT01P")
res[, c("group", "br", "adm", "br_diff", "br_ref", "adm_ref", "ntb", "wr")]
rules <- data.frame(statistic = c("br_diff", "br_ref", "ntb", "wr"),
                    threshold = c(0.05, 0.5, 0.1, 1.5))
sel <- vapply(seq_len(nrow(rules)), function(i) {
  oc <- SelectionOC(res, rules$statistic[i], threshold = rules$threshold[i])
  oc$group[oc$p_select == 1]
}, character(1))
data.frame(rules, selected = sel)
```

## Note

The data of this article are invented for illustration. They are generated by
the script `data-raw/make_example_trial.py` of the GitHub repository of the
package.
